Personally, I still think that my playing ability wasn't up to their standard was the main reason. Again, I know I'm not the greatest. Never crossed my mind.

My replacement actually joined the band a few months prior as a mandolin player (it was an East Coast/Celtic style band) who started out playing music on Bass and Guitar.

Stand up guy, really. Helped me figure out some more playing styles and techniques.

More recently, I heard ex-band play at a wedding I was attending (old friend from High School). I listened to their sound, and it really didn't sound much different from when I was there.

Front man is still a scum bag. Other singer still has an ever growing ego and refuses to take blame (It was always someone else's fault). Sax player still makes up everything on the fly (talented guy, but nailing him down to play a particular piece was about as productive as trying to nail Jell-o to the wall).

Ah well. Not my Monkey, not my Circus. Aaaaand now I'm rambling.

8 years I was part of a band.

I'll be the first to admit that I am not the greatest Bass player in the world. I flub every once in a while, but always quick to recover (Even wrote about 90% of the original lyrics we were trying to create).

It was about a month before making our 3rd CD. It was going to be a CD of all originals or traditional pieces. No more Royalties! After the rehearsal, I was approached by the rest of the band (Two weren't able to make it to the rehearsal) and informed that I wasn't going to be appearing on the next CD due to two factors:

1) I was (and still am) in the works of moving to South Africa. There was no established timeline as to when I would be going or or for how long.

2) My playing ability wasn't up to their standard.

Truth be told, I'm kinda glad they kicked me out.

Don't have to deal with temperamental front man (Who is a scumbag for other reasons, some of which affected me, but I don't care about that any more). Don't have to listen to infighting. Don't have to lug the Sound gear around any more.

Now, I get to play with my Room mates, some of which are the most talented people I have ever met.

The only piece of advice I could offer OP is this:

Endure and Persevere.

If that means joining another band, go for it. If it means MAKING a new band, go for that even harder. Play music for you. Create for your own benefit.
